att.title: Attendance management
att.subtitle: Track attendance, leave, overtime and business trips

colors.desc: 3-layer color tokens: primitive → semantic → component. Components use semantic only. Light/Dark swaps semantic values only.

icons.desc: The full ~5900 Tabler icon set — the project icon standard. Prefer object mode: <tabler-icon [icon]="IconTruck" /> (no registration, tree-shakeable, typo = compile error). String mode <tabler-icon icon="truck" /> needs registration for dynamic names. Components pick a meaning-fit icon from the whole set.

spacing.desc: 4px spacing system. Icon/control/avatar sizes, radius, border width.

elevation.desc: Shadow (subtle, functional), z-index scale, motion duration/easing.
elevation.motionHint: Motion — hover a track to see easing

components.emptyBody: Build a component in hrm-ui, then add a gallery page here: every variant × state (default/hover/focus/disabled/selected/error/loading), viewed side by side in Light + Dark.

nz.desc: ng-zorro components mapped to design tokens. Change brand/theme/radius/font in config → ng-zorro follows automatically (no hardcoding).

hrm.desc: hrm-ui WRAPPER components (P0) — clean API (variant/size/status), wrapping ng-zorro + design tokens, ngModel/formControl support. These are 'our own' components modules install and use, not raw ng-zorro.

button.desc: A button lets users perform an action: save, delete, submit, approve…
button.purpose: Let users perform a clear action (save, delete, submit, approve…).
button.behavior: Clicking runs the action immediately. Primary stands out most — only one Primary per area. Default for secondary actions.
button.avoid: Pure page navigation — use a link or menu instead.
button.when1: At the end of a form to save or cancel
button.when2: Primary action on a screen or toolbar
button.do1: Only one Primary for the main action per screen/group; use Default or Text for the rest.
button.do2: Button text describes the exact action ("Save changes", "Delete account"), not vague ("OK", "Submit").
button.do3: Slow actions (save/submit) show a loading state so users know it is running.
button.do4: Icon-only buttons must have an ariaLabel + tooltip for sighted users.
button.dont1: Multiple Primary buttons on one screen — focus is lost.
button.dont2: Using Danger for an irreversible action without a confirmation step.
button.dont3: Using a button for pure navigation — use a link.
button.exSizeD: Small / medium / large side by side. Small for dense UI like toolbars; medium for most cases; large for a prominent CTA.
button.exVarD: Button styles in normal / disabled / loading states. Primary for the main action, Default for secondary, Text–Link low emphasis, Danger for dangerous actions.
button.exIconD: A leading icon boosts action recognition. Use it when the icon speeds recognition — plus for 'Add', trash for 'Delete'.
button.exIconOnlyD: Square icon-only buttons (ariaLabel required for screen readers) for tight toolbars. Block spans 100% width for narrow forms, mobile or modals.
button.title: Button

avatar.desc: A photo, initials, or icon representing an employee or a project team.
avatar.purpose: Quickly identify an employee or project team within a list, card, or comment.
avatar.behavior: Shows the photo first; if there is no photo, shows the name initials; if there is no name either, shows the default person icon.
avatar.avoid: Using it for logos, product images, or illustrations — it is only for people or teams.
avatar.when1: Showing an employee in a list or card
avatar.when2: Next to a name in comments or messages
avatar.do1: Always include a name so initials show when the photo fails and screen readers can tell who it is.
avatar.do2: Choose a size that fits the context: small for dense lists, large for profile pages.
avatar.do3: When grouped, let the avatars overlap slightly to save space while each face stays visible.
avatar.dont1: Use an avatar that is too small in a dense table — it loses its identifying value.
avatar.exPhotoD: Shows the employee's profile photo. Use it when an image URL is available; if the image fails, it falls back to initials.
avatar.exInitialsD: Shows the name initials instead of a photo. Use it when only the employee's name is available, such as a new account with no profile photo loaded yet.
avatar.exColorfulD: Enable colorful: each name automatically takes one of 8 colors (solid background, white text) from tokens — to distinguish people in a list and avoid monotony. The same name always yields the same color.
avatar.exIconD: Shows a person icon when there is neither a photo nor a name — such as an anonymous profile or a placeholder before the employee is known.
avatar.exSizeD: Small for inline name mentions, medium for lists and cards, large for the header of an employee profile page.
avatar.exShapeD: Circle for people (default), rounded square for project teams or departments to distinguish them from individuals.
avatar.exGroupD: Stack several overlapping avatars into one row with the Avatar Group component — beyond the limit it collapses into '+N'. See the dedicated page for full examples.
avatar.title: Avatar

avatarGroup.desc: Stack several overlapping avatars into one compact row — project participants, an approval chain.
avatarGroup.purpose: Show A GROUP of people within the space of one cell/row: who is participating, who approves.
avatarGroup.behavior: Each avatar overlaps the next, with a background ring to separate the layers. Beyond the max limit, the remainder collapses into a '+N' slot. Without a photo, it shows initials colored by name.
avatarGroup.avoid: A list of people where each name must be read — use a table with a User Cell instead.
avatarGroup.when1: A "Participants" column in a project table
avatarGroup.when2: An approval chain on a request card
avatarGroup.when3: The footer of a project card — who is on the team
avatarGroup.do1: Limit max to 3–5 avatars — too long loses the "quick glance" purpose.
avatarGroup.do2: Pass a full name to get stable initials and color when a photo is missing.
avatarGroup.dont1: Use it for a single person — use a regular Avatar.
avatarGroup.exBasicD: A group of project participants. If a photo is available it shows the photo; otherwise, initials colored by name.
avatarGroup.exLimitD: max=3: shows only the first 3 people, the rest collapse into '+N' — saving space in tables and cards.
avatarGroup.exCompactD: Smaller and more tightly overlapped — for dense table rows or card footers where space is tight.
avatarGroup.exSizeD: Set the size by context: 24 for table rows, 32 by default, 40 for the header of a project card.
avatarGroup.title: Avatar Group

tag.desc: A short colored label to categorize an item by group or show its status, readable at a glance when scanning a list.
tag.purpose: Attach a short label to categorize an item by group (department, request type, priority) or show its status (approved, pending, rejected).
tag.behavior: Color CARRIES MEANING: it is either a labeled category group or a status (green/yellow/red). A tag can have a close button to remove it — typically used for applied filters.
tag.avoid: Coloring purely for decoration with no meaning; or repeating the same label on every row so it no longer adds any information.
tag.when1: Categorizing by group: department, leave type, priority, contract type
tag.when2: Showing the status of a request/record (approved, pending, rejected)
tag.when3: An applied filter label (with a close button to remove it)
tag.do1: Use the categorical palette (blue, purple, teal…) for groups: department names, content types, priority levels.
tag.do2: Use status colors (green/yellow/red) with their true meaning and only for statuses that need attention: pending, rejected, overdue.
tag.do3: Keep the text in a tag short — a few words; long details belong in the surrounding description.
tag.dont1: Assign colors arbitrarily without a convention — the same meaning in a different color each time.
tag.dont2: Repeat the same label on every row of a table — if every row says "Active", no tag stands out.
tag.exColorsD: Attach colored labels to groups such as departments, priority levels, or request types; use the palette to tell groups apart visually.
tag.exPaletteD: Ten colors with no status meaning, reserved for grouping; light background, always-legible text, adapts automatically to Light/Dark themes.
tag.exStatusD: Show the status of an item such as Approved, Pending, or Rejected; use it in table rows, list items, or detail pages to see it immediately at a glance.
tag.exCloseableD: A label with a close button for users to remove it; typically used for applied filters on a table or search results.
tag.title: Tag

badge.desc: A colored label to categorize, a small number to count, or a dot to signal status.
badge.purpose: Quickly mark an item with a color, number, or dot so viewers recognize it immediately when scanning a list or table.
badge.behavior: Colored labels group items; a number counts unhandled items (over the threshold it shows '99+'); a colored dot signals status.
badge.avoid: Coloring purely for decoration, or leaving a number too large without abbreviating it.
badge.when1: Categorizing by group with colored labels (department, priority, topic)
badge.when2: Counting unread/pending items next to an icon or menu
badge.do1: Use colored labels for categorization and provide a color legend the first time.
badge.do2: Use a number for unread/unhandled items; a colored dot for status.
badge.do3: Keep the text in a label short — a few words.
badge.dont1: Assign colors arbitrarily without a convention, the same meaning in a different color each time.
badge.dont2: Show numbers in the thousands without abbreviating them.
badge.exColorsD: Attach colored labels to groups such as departments, priority levels, or topics; use the palette to tell groups apart visually.
badge.exCountD: Show a number on the badge to report notifications, unread messages, or a total count of items; place it next to an icon, menu item, or list label.
badge.exStatusD: Show the status of an item such as Active / Pending / Error; use it in table rows, list items, or detail pages.
badge.title: Badge

card.desc: A block that gathers related information into one tidy panel, with a title and a thin border.
card.purpose: Gather a cluster of related information or actions into one tidy block that is easy to scan.
card.behavior: Has a title, a thin border, and rounded corners; it can brighten on hover. A muted background is for secondary notes, a colored background for quick categorization by group/project.
card.avoid: Nesting cards within cards across many levels — it becomes cluttered and the main block is hard to spot.
card.when1: A profile or metric card on a dashboard
card.when2: Gathering related information into a block
card.when3: Notes, tips, or supporting information in a sidebar
card.do1: Gather genuinely related information into one card (employee card, metric card, project card).
card.do2: Use a muted background for notes, tips, and supporting information — distinct yet unobtrusive.
card.do3: Place action buttons in the card footer, aligned to the right so the eye finds them easily.
card.dont1: Nest many cards within each other or apply decorative colors that carry no categorical meaning.
card.exHeadD: The standard frame around a chart or list: a rounded icon tile plus a bold title (with optional subtitle), and a right-hand action area via the [cardActions] slot — filter/sort buttons, ⋮, a period dropdown, a See all link.
card.exVariantsD: A plain white card, a muted card, and colored cards placed side by side; a colored background enables quick categorization by group or project and adapts automatically to light/dark themes.
card.cardMutedB: Muted background, recedes into the back.
card.exLayoutD: A card with a title, body, and footer holding action buttons; suitable for forms, dialogs, or settings panels that need clearly divided sections with buttons aligned to the right.
card.exNoteD: A muted-background card for tips, notes, or supporting information; prominent just enough while still receding, suitable for a help block in a sidebar or inserted between content.
card.tipBody: You can filter the employee list by department using the search box above to work faster.
card.exClickD: The whole card is a button: pointer cursor, a slight lift on hover, a focus ring for keyboard use. Use it for navigation cards — clicking opens the detail screen.
card.clickBody1: Click to open the detail screen · clicked
card.exSelectD: The card acts as a selection box: click to select/deselect — the border turns the primary color and a check mark appears in the corner. Use it when a choice needs more than a single radio line: registering a work shift, choosing a request type.
card.title: Card

collapse.desc: A group of content that can collapse/expand behind a header to keep the screen tidy and readable.
collapse.ovPersonalB: The employee's full name, date of birth, gender, ID number, and contact details.
collapse.ovContractB: Contract type, term, start date, and the agreed salary.
collapse.ovHistoryB: History of departments, job titles, and transfers.
collapse.purpose: Hide secondary content behind a header, letting users expand it when needed — keeping the page tidy and scannable.
collapse.behavior: Click a header to expand or collapse a panel; the arrow rotates with the state. The 'single panel open' style aids focus, the 'multiple panels open' style aids comparison.
collapse.avoid: Collapsing important or required information — users may not expand it and miss it.
collapse.when1: A long profile split into multiple sections
collapse.when2: A settings page or frequently asked questions (FAQ)
collapse.when3: A detail section within a screen that needs to stay tidy
collapse.do1: Use the single panel open (accordion) style for settings pages or FAQs, where only one panel should be viewed at a time.
collapse.do2: Use the multiple panels open style when users need to compare content across panels (benefit lists, plans).
collapse.do3: Expand (active) the important panel on first view — do not force users to click to see core information.
collapse.dont1: Collapse important or required information — users may not discover it.
collapse.dont2: Nest collapses beyond two levels — content becomes hard to find and navigate.
collapse.dont3: Use a collapse for a short paragraph — showing the content directly is better.
collapse.exSingleD: Only one panel can be open at a time; opening a new one collapses the currently open panel. Use it for settings pages or FAQs where focus on one panel is preferable.
collapse.faq1H: How do I submit a leave request?
collapse.faq1B: Go to the Leave section, choose the leave type and date range, then send it to your manager for approval.
collapse.faq2B: Payslips are released on the 5th of each month and sent via the employee portal.
collapse.faq3H: Where do I update my personal information?
collapse.faq3B: In My Profile, open the Personal Information section and click Edit.
collapse.exMultiD: Multiple panels can be open at once. Use it when users need to compare content across panels, such as comparing benefits between employee groups.
collapse.ben1B: Full insurance, 12 annual leave days, a 13th-month bonus, and periodic health checkups.
collapse.ben2B: 85% of salary, a lunch allowance; annual leave and bonuses do not yet apply.
collapse.ben3B: Project-based pay, flexible working hours, no fixed-hour commitment.
collapse.exGhostD: Panels are separated by lines instead of a bordered frame. Use it for detail sections in a side panel or secondary bar, where a bordered frame would make the interface feel heavy.
collapse.addrB: House number, street, ward, district, and province per household registration.
collapse.emgB: The relative's full name, relationship, and phone number to contact when needed.
collapse.bankB: Bank name, account number, and branch used to pay salary.
collapse.exDefaultT: Collapse — Open by default & locked panels
collapse.exDefaultD: Expand the panel to view right away on entry, and lock panels not yet due so users do not open them by mistake.
collapse.step1B: The candidate profile is complete: full name, applied position, and interview date.
collapse.step2B: The proposed salary, expected start date, and approver.
collapse.step3B: Will unlock after the candidate accepts the job offer.
collapse.title: Collapse

carousel.desc: Displays slides one at a time in the same spot: banners, announcements, intro images.
carousel.purpose: Present a few peer-level pieces of content one at a time in the same spot (homepage banner, a series of announcements, intro images).
carousel.behavior: Users switch slides via navigation dots, arrows, or let it autoplay. Only one slide is visible at a time.
carousel.avoid: Placing must-see information in a carousel — many people do not click to later slides, so it is easily missed.
carousel.when1: A homepage banner rotating a few items of news
carousel.when2: A few-step onboarding for new employees
carousel.when3: A series of announcements or short intro images
carousel.do1: Use it for banners, onboarding, announcements — peer-level content with few slides.
carousel.do2: Keep the navigation dots so users know there are more slides and which one they are on.
carousel.do3: Give slides the same height so the frame does not jump when switching.
carousel.dont1: Place important must-see information here — put it right on the page, do not hide it in a slide.
carousel.dont2: Autoplay too fast so users switch slides before finishing reading.
carousel.exDotsD: By default there is a row of dots below indicating the number of slides and the current position. Users click a dot to jump to the desired slide.
carousel.exAutoplayD: Automatically switches slides after a few seconds, suitable for a homepage banner rotating a few items of news. Users can still click a dot to view any slide.
carousel.exFadeD: Slides transition by fading rather than sliding sideways. A gentle feel, suitable for image banners or greetings.
carousel.exArrowsD: Add previous/next arrows to move one slide at a time, handy when users want to browse in sequence themselves rather than wait for autoplay.
carousel.title: Carousel

calendar.desc: A full-month (or full-year) grid to view dates in context and mark status: attendance, days off, holidays, events.
calendar.purpose: See a full month/year overview and mark each day's status (working, off, holiday, event).
calendar.behavior: Shows a whole month in a 7-column grid; click the arrows to change months, click a day to select it. Each day cell can render extra status marks/labels. Switch to year mode to see 12 months at once.
calendar.avoid: Just entering a single date in a form — a Date Picker is more compact and takes less space.
calendar.do1: Mark status right in the day cell (dot + label) so the whole month reads at a single glance.
calendar.do2: Explain what the colors/marks mean (off, holiday, event) — do not leave viewers guessing.
calendar.do3: Use year mode when you need to see year-long trends (leave, quarterly book closing).
calendar.do4: Embed the compact version (not fullscreen) into a card/profile when the calendar is only supporting information.
calendar.dont1: Use the calendar to enter a date of birth or a far-off date — a text field/Date Picker is faster.
calendar.dont2: Color many days at once without a legend — viewers will not understand why.
calendar.exMonthD: A full-month attendance sheet: weekends dimmed, holidays tagged in red. One look and the block of days off is immediately visible — suitable for a department's work/leave overview.
calendar.exYearD: A grid of 12 months in a year. Use it when you need the big picture: leave distribution, quarterly book closing, quickly picking a month to view details.
calendar.exEventT: Calendar — Day cells with event badges
calendar.exEventD: Each day cell shows that day's events (meetings, interviews, deadlines) with a status dot + short label. Viewers scan the whole month while still grasping the work schedule.
calendar.exCompactD: A mini version (not fullscreen) that fits a narrow card — embed it into an employee profile or sidebar when the calendar is only supporting information, not the page's main content.
calendar.title: Calendar

statCard.desc: A fixed-height 96px KPI cell for dashboards: icon, large number, label, change delta. Two styles — white background (default) and a multicolor gradient background.
statCard.purpose: Bring the most important numbers to the top of the screen for a quick read of the situation — one metric per card.
statCard.behavior: Fixed height of 96px, arranged in an even row. The default white style suits serious dashboards; the multicolor gradient style highlights a standout group of metrics. Tabler icons; in the gradient style the icon also shows an enlarged faded copy in the corner.
statCard.avoid: Cramming too many secondary numbers into one card; mixing the two styles messily in the same row.
statCard.when1: The top KPI row of a dashboard
statCard.when2: Highlighting a standout group of metrics
statCard.when3: A quick summary of a single metric
statCard.do1: Arrange 3–4 cards per row; keep the same style within each row for consistency.
statCard.do2: Gradient style for the "highlight" row at the top; default for the detailed number blocks below.
statCard.dont1: Use status/gradient colors against their meaning (a decrease colored green).
statCard.title: Stat Card

timeline.desc: Presents the milestones/events of a record or process in chronological order.
timeline.purpose: Show users how a record or process unfolds over time — which steps are done, which are pending.
timeline.behavior: Milestones are stacked vertically in chronological order; the dot color shows each milestone's status. They can alternate on both sides when each milestone carries more information.
timeline.avoid: Data with no chronological order — use a list or table.
timeline.do1: Use it for employee record history, multi-level approval flows, and activity logs.
timeline.do2: Use consistent dot colors by status (green = done, blue = in progress, gray = pending, red = rejected/error).
timeline.do3: Order milestones strictly by time, with the oldest on top.
timeline.dont1: Use it for non-sequential data, or lists meant only to enumerate.
timeline.dont2: Apply many colors that carry no status meaning — it becomes cluttered and hard to read.
timeline.ex1D: How a record progresses from application to becoming a full-time employee. Each milestone is a completed step in the HR lifecycle.
timeline.ex2D: The dot color reveals each milestone's status: green completed, blue in progress, red rejected. A glance at the color tells the situation.
timeline.ex3D: The gray milestone at the end is a step not yet reached, still awaiting processing. It shows the approver exactly where the request is stuck.
timeline.ex4D: Milestones alternate on both sides of the axis. Suitable when each milestone carries more information, spreading content out for easier reading.
timeline.title: Timeline

comment.desc: Displays a user's remark: the author, time, and content.
comment.purpose: Present a user's opinion, note, or discussion attached to an item (request, record, document).
comment.behavior: Each comment has an avatar + author name + time + content. It can include actions (Reply, Like) and nested replies below.
comment.avoid: Recording system milestones/events in chronological order — use the Timeline.
comment.when2: Discussion and exchange on a record or document
comment.when3: Back-and-forth replies between an employee and a manager
comment.do1: Use it for discussion threads, approval remarks, or person-to-person exchanges.
comment.do2: Place replies nested below the original comment to keep the conversation flow clear.
comment.do3: Show easy-to-read times ("2 hours ago", "Yesterday") so readers can follow what happened.
comment.dont1: Use it to record system logs or automatic change history.
comment.ovBody: Approval remark — leave is granted, remember to hand over your work before you go.
comment.ex1D: An approver's remark attached to a leave request: who commented, when, and what they said.
comment.ex1Body: The 3-day leave request is reasonable. Please add a medical certificate before I give final approval.
comment.ex2D: The original comment and the replies below it, indented to show clearly who is replying to whom on a request.
comment.ex2Body1: Have you arranged who will cover for you during these 3 days off?
comment.ex2Body2: Yes, I've asked Phuc to cover for me and finished handing over the documents.
comment.ex2Body3: All good, I'll approve the request.
comment.ex3D: A comment with actions below it (Reply, Like) so readers can interact right within the discussion thread.
comment.ex3Body: Proposal to allow carrying over up to 5 days of annual leave — what does everyone think?
comment.title: Comment

statistic.desc: Highlights one important number so leaders can grasp it quickly on a dashboard.
statistic.purpose: Highlight a key metric so viewers grasp it quickly without reading a data table.
statistic.behavior: The number is shown large and bold with a label. You can add a prefix/suffix (₫, %, +) and color the number when it carries a good or warning meaning.
statistic.avoid: Cramming too many metrics on one row — viewers can't tell which number matters.
statistic.when1: A prominent metric tile on a dashboard
statistic.when2: Summarizing KPIs / key figures for the period
statistic.when3: A quick up-vs-down comparison against the previous period
statistic.do1: Pair each number with a short, clear label (Total headcount, Monthly payroll).
statistic.do2: Add a unit symbol (₫, %, people) so the number speaks for itself.
statistic.do3: Only color a number when it carries a status — green is good, red needs attention.
statistic.dont1: Placing too many metrics side by side so none of them stands out.
statistic.dont2: Applying decorative color to neutral numbers — it's easily mistaken for a warning.
statistic.ovD: One large number with a short label. Use it for overview metric tiles on an HR dashboard.
statistic.ex1D: Add a ₫ suffix for money, a % sign for ratios. The attached unit makes the number instantly understandable, no caption needed.
statistic.ex2D: The arrow and color show whether a metric is improving or worsening versus the previous period — a green up arrow is positive, a red down arrow needs attention.
statistic.ex3D: Amber coloring flags a metric sitting at a threshold worth watching, for example a backlog of requests pending approval.
statistic.title: Statistic

empty.desc: Shown when an area has no data yet — with the reason and the next step for the user.
empty.purpose: Tell users why an area is empty and what to do next — an empty list, a search with no results, or a first-time setup.
empty.behavior: Shows an illustration + a description line; usually with 1–2 action buttons to leave the empty state (create new, clear filters).
empty.avoid: Using it for an error that needs immediate action — use a Banner/Alert instead of an Empty state.
empty.when1: A table or list with no data yet
empty.when3: A first-time setup screen with nothing created yet
empty.do1: State clearly what is empty + one action button ("Add employee") so users know how to proceed.
empty.do2: Use an image/icon that fits the context (a people icon for a staff list, a request icon for a request list).
empty.dont1: Leaving a blank screen with no explanation — always say what happened and what to do next.
empty.dont2: Using a generic description like "No data" — state specifically what is empty and why.
empty.ex1D: The default illustration with one specific description line. Use it when a table or list has no data yet and you only need to say what is empty.
empty.ex2D: Four common empty contexts, each with its own icon: no data, no results, load error, first use (inviting creation). The description is still set by the screen.
empty.ex3D: A full empty state: image, description, and action button. Use it when a search returns nothing or a list was just cleared — the button gives users a way forward.
empty.ex4D: Replace the default image with a context-fitting icon (employees, requests). It helps users recognize what list this is before reading the description.
empty.ex4Users: No employees in this department yet
empty.ex5D: Place the empty state inside a card for a first-time setup or onboarding screen. Use it when the user hasn't created any item — the card fills up as they take action.
empty.ex5Desc: No employees yet — add the first person to get started
empty.title: Empty

image.desc: Displays a profile photo, document, or record image; click to view it enlarged.
image.purpose: Display a specific image (a profile portrait, a document photo, an attached record) and allow a larger view when needed.
image.behavior: Click the image to open a full-screen enlarged view. If the image fails or is missing, a fallback image shows instead of a broken empty box.
image.avoid: Using it for the round avatar of a person in a list — that belongs to the Avatar.
image.when1: A portrait photo in an employee record
image.when2: Viewing attached document and paperwork images
image.when3: A group of document images that need enlarging to read details
image.do1: Set a fixed size (width and height) so the page doesn't shift layout while the image loads.
image.do2: Always provide an image description (alt) so screen reader users know what the image is.
image.do3: Only enable zoom for images that need detail (paperwork, records); turn it off for small decorative images.
image.dont1: Cramming heavy, unoptimized original images into a long list — it's slow and burns data.
image.ex1D: A portrait photo in an employee record, at a fixed size for a stable layout. Use it at the top of a personal information page.
image.ex2D: Click the image to open a full-screen large view. Use it for records or paperwork that need careful reading.
image.ex3D: When the image path is broken or missing, the system shows a fallback image instead of a broken empty box — users still see a tidy frame.
image.ex4D: Several document images (ID card, diploma, contract) placed side by side; each is clickable to zoom individually.
image.title: Image

list.desc: A collection of items stacked vertically, each with a title and short description — for staff lists, recent activity, settings items.
list.purpose: Present a group of related items in rows — each item has a title and description, optionally an avatar or right-aligned secondary content.
list.behavior: Items are stacked vertically, evenly spaced, with dividers between them. You can attach a header for the whole list and a footer note summarizing it.
list.avoid: Multi-column data that needs sorting/filtering — use a Grid. A single standalone item or unrelated, scattered content.
list.when1: Staff lists, recent activity, settings items
list.when2: Each item has a title + description, optionally an avatar or status
list.when3: No need to sort/filter across many columns
list.do1: Attach a header to the list to state clearly what it is (this also helps screen readers).
list.do2: Use the leading/trailing item slot for an avatar, icon, or status label — for quick recognition of each item.
list.dont1: Mixing clickable and non-clickable items in the same list without clearly distinguishing them.
list.dont2: Using a list for a single standalone item or to lay out unrelated content.
list.ex1D: A simple list, each item with a title and description. Good for staff lists or settings items.
list.ex2D: Each item has an initials avatar at the front, with a title and job title — for quick recognition of employees in a list.
list.ex3D: Each item has a secondary label on the right: an employee's work status or recent activity time.
list.ex4D: The header labels the whole list; the footer adds a summary note. Use it when the list needs clear context.
list.title: List

descriptions.desc: A label–value table for viewing the details of a record, request, or entry.
descriptions.purpose: Present the detailed information of a record as label : value pairs, readable and compact.
descriptions.behavior: Each item has a label and a value; they can be laid out in multiple columns or with the label above the value. Borders can be turned on to separate cells clearly.
descriptions.avoid: Presenting many records at once as a list — use a Grid.
descriptions.when2: Viewing the details of a request or record
descriptions.when3: An information summary block in a sidebar
descriptions.do1: Place the label beside the value when it's short (code, date); place the label above when the value is long or complex.
descriptions.do2: Use it for detail screens: employee records, leave requests, contract details.
descriptions.dont1: Using it to enter many fields — use a Form layout instead.
descriptions.dont2: Using it for data that has no clear label : value structure.
descriptions.ex1D: A single-column list, one label : value pair per row. Use it for a compact summary block in a detail screen.
descriptions.ex2D: A bordered multi-column grid, packing lots of information into one block. Fits a full record detail page.
descriptions.ex3D: The label sits on top, the value below. Use it when values are long, like an address or notes, readable at any screen width.
descriptions.ex4D: Small size, no borders, for a secondary block or sidebar where space is tight.
descriptions.title: Descriptions

timestamp.desc: Shows time relatively — '3 hours ago', 'yesterday' — easier to feel than a full date-time; hover to see the exact time.
timestamp.purpose: Answer 'how long ago?' instantly — the brain processes 'just now' faster than '08/07/2026 14:32'.
timestamp.behavior: Automatically changes unit by distance (seconds → minutes → hours → days → months → years) and refreshes every minute. By default, hovering shows the full absolute time.
timestamp.avoid: Records and reports that need an exact moment for reconciliation — use a full date-time (absolute mode).
timestamp.when2: A "last updated" column in a record table
timestamp.when3: A secondary line under a Date Cell
timestamp.do1: Use it for recent activity (comments, logs, notifications); past 1 month, consider showing a specific date.
timestamp.do2: Keep mode='both' — those who need precision can still check via the tooltip.
timestamp.dont1: Using it in timekeeping/payroll tables — those need an absolute date-time.
timestamp.ex1D: relative shows only the relative text; absolute shows only the full time; both (default) = relative + a full-time tooltip (the dotted underline hints to hover).
timestamp.ex2D: The unit changes automatically with the time distance — no configuration needed.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

input.desc: A field for users to type a single line of text: name, code, email, phone number.
input.ovHelp: Type an employee name or code
input.purpose: Let users enter a short single line of information (full name, employee code, email, phone number).
input.behavior: Saves as you type. On error, the border turns red with an error message below. The placeholder hint disappears once you start typing.
input.avoid: Entering long multi-line text — use Textarea instead.
input.when1: Entering short single-line information in a form
input.do1: Always keep a visible label; only hide it when the context is clear (a search box with a magnifier icon).
input.do2: On error, state exactly what's wrong ("Email must contain @") instead of just a red border.
input.do3: Match the field size to the content length — small for codes, large for URLs.
input.dont1: Use a placeholder in place of a label — it disappears while typing and is hard to recall.
input.exIconD: A leading icon hints at what to enter — a lock for passwords, an envelope for email. It helps users recognize the field faster.
input.exSearchD: A search box with a hidden label, a magnifier icon and a clear button. Use it for search bars in a toolbar/header where the icon already gives enough context.
input.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for dense UI (table filters), medium for most forms, large for a standout single-field page.
input.exStateD: Error, warning and success with a message. Tell users what's wrong and how to fix it — 'Email must contain @' beats a plain red border; a green border confirms it's valid.
input.exTypeD: Text, password and email types; plus field-level features: required/optional label, description, read-only.
input.title: Input

inputNumber.desc: A numeric field with increment/decrement buttons, a min–max range and a unit: leave days, quantity, percentage.
inputNumber.purpose: Let users enter a number (leave days, quantity, age, percentage…).
inputNumber.behavior: Click the arrows to increase/decrease, or type directly. Values outside the min–max range are blocked. The unit shows inside the field so users know what the number refers to.
inputNumber.avoid: Entering money amounts — use the Money field to add thousands separators and the ₫ unit automatically.
inputNumber.when2: Fields with a clear value range (0–100, 0–12…)
inputNumber.when3: Numbers that need a unit (%, hours, days)
inputNumber.do1: Set min/max limits and a step that fit the business logic (e.g. leave days 0–12, step 1).
inputNumber.do2: Show the unit ("%", "days", "hours") so users know what the number means.
inputNumber.dont1: Use a text field for numbers — you lose the steppers and risk invalid formats.
inputNumber.dont2: Mark a field as both "required" and "optional" at once — they contradict each other.
inputNumber.exStateD: A numeric field in error, warning and success states with a message — telling users what's wrong and how to fix it, or confirming the value is valid.
inputNumber.helpAge: Please double-check; under 18 requires a permit
inputNumber.exRangeD: A numeric field with a min–max limit and a helper line — guiding users to enter within the allowed range.
inputNumber.exUnitD: A numeric field with a percent suffix and a valid range — users instantly know what the number means.
inputNumber.exIntD: An integer field with a unit and limits — for day counts and quantities that must stay within range.
inputNumber.title: Number Input

textarea.desc: A field for users to enter long text — reasons, descriptions, notes — that grows with the number of lines.
textarea.ovHelp: Type your content; the field grows taller as you add lines
textarea.purpose: Let users enter long, multi-line text: leave reasons, job descriptions, review notes.
textarea.behavior: Saves as you type. The field grows taller as you add lines (within the row limit). You can enable a character counter; on error, the border turns red with an error message below.
textarea.avoid: Entering short single-line information (full name, employee code) — use Input instead.
textarea.when1: Entering long multi-line reasons, descriptions, notes
textarea.when2: Content with a character limit to track
textarea.do1: Set a sensible visible row count (3–4 rows) to show enough content without filling the screen.
textarea.do2: When there's a character limit, enable the counter so users know how much room is left before text is cut.
textarea.do3: On error, state exactly what's wrong ("Please enter a reason") instead of just a red border.
textarea.dont1: Use it for single-line data — it clutters and wastes space.
textarea.exCountD: A field with a character limit and a live counter in the corner; when you type past the limit, the counter turns red to warn you.
textarea.exStateD: Required, disabled and read-only fields side by side — showing the states the field supports.
textarea.exValidD: Error, warning and success states with a message — immediate feedback as the user types: red when missing, amber when it needs attention, green when entered correctly.
textarea.helpShort: A bit short, consider adding more
textarea.sampleLeave: My child is ill; I'm requesting one day off to care for them.
textarea.exResizeD: resize='vertical': turns off auto-grow, the field stays fixed at minRows and users drag the bottom-right corner to expand — good for unpredictable long content. Use resize='none' to lock the size.
textarea.phResizeV: Drag the bottom-right corner to resize vertically…
textarea.exIconD: A field with an icon on the label hinting at the content type — a chat bubble for messages, a pencil for notes — helping users recognize the field faster.
textarea.title: Textarea

checkbox.desc: A box to turn one option on/off, or to select multiple items at once.
checkbox.purpose: Let users check/uncheck one item, or select several independent items in a list.
checkbox.behavior: Click the box or the label to toggle. Multiple boxes are independent. The 'select all' box shows a dash when only part of the list is checked.
checkbox.avoid: Choosing one among mutually exclusive options — use Radio.
checkbox.when1: Selecting multiple items in a list
checkbox.when3: Bulk-selecting to export records or assign permissions
checkbox.do1: Keep the label clear, and make the whole label clickable.
checkbox.do2: Long lists should have a "select all" box for bulk actions.
checkbox.dont1: Use it for an instantly-applied on/off toggle — use Switch.
checkbox.exAllD: The 'select all' box at the top of the list turns into a dash when only some items are checked — used for bulk actions like exporting records or assigning permissions.
checkbox.exEndD: A secondary label (price or status) at the end of each row adds context without cluttering the main label, helping users compare quickly.
checkbox.title: Checkbox

radio.desc: Let users pick exactly one of a few mutually exclusive options.
radio.ovHelp: Choose the time range to view
radio.purpose: Let users pick a single option within a mutually exclusive group.
radio.behavior: Picking one option automatically deselects the others. All options stay visible for direct comparison.
radio.avoid: More than 5–6 options — use a Select instead to keep it compact.
radio.when2: Needing to see all options at once to compare
radio.when3: Required fields where a sensible default should be preselected
radio.do1: Use it for 2–5 options that need to be visible all at once.
radio.do2: Always preselect a sensible default so users have less to click.
radio.do3: Order the options in an intuitive way (ascending, most common first).
radio.dont1: Use it for selecting several options at once — that's Checkbox's job.
radio.exHorizD: Options laid out in a single horizontal row, tidy for small groups like filters or quick picks on a toolbar.
radio.exPlanD: A list of plans with the price shown right on each option, helping users compare and pick the right plan at a glance.
radio.exDescD: The group has one shared guidance line, and each option carries a short explanation so users understand the differences before choosing.
radio.helpWorkMode: Choose the work arrangement that applies to this employee
radio.exReqD: Required field: if the user hasn't picked any option, an error line appears below so they know they must choose before saving.
radio.modeOffice: On-site — present for all working days
radio.modeHybrid: Hybrid — a few days in the office, a few days remote
radio.modeRemote: Remote — working entirely without coming to the office
radio.title: Radio

switch.desc: Flip a state on/off, applied immediately.
switch.purpose: Quickly turn a feature or state on/off, applied instantly.
switch.behavior: Flipping it changes the state immediately, no Save needed. The on state shows an accent color, off returns to gray.
switch.avoid: A choice that only applies after clicking Save — use Checkbox.
switch.when1: Turning a feature on/off with immediate effect
switch.when3: A settings panel with many on-off options
switch.do1: Use it for instant on/off toggles (activating an account, receiving notifications).
switch.do2: Always keep a label that says exactly what the switch controls; add a description if the consequences need explaining.
switch.dont1: Use it for multi-value choices or ones that need a confirmation step.
switch.exDescD: A switch with a label and a description line explaining what happens when it's on, reassuring users as they act.
switch.emailNotifyDesc: Send an email whenever a request needs your approval.
switch.exPanelD: Several switches arranged in a settings card, label on the left and switch on the right, easy to scan and adjust one by one.
switch.exDisabledD: A disabled switch with a label and description, used for a feature that isn't available yet or requires a plan upgrade to enable.
switch.twoFaDesc: Available on the Enterprise plan — contact your administrator to enable.
switch.exStateD: A switch placed in a validated field: when it must be on but is off, a red reminder line appears below.
switch.agreeTerms: Agree to the terms of use
switch.errAgree: You need to turn this on to continue.
switch.helpSync: Enabled — data will sync automatically every night.
switch.title: Switch

segmented.desc: A row of joined buttons to quickly pick one of a few views or filters; exactly one item is always selected.
segmented.purpose: Let users quickly pick one of 2–5 mutually exclusive views or filters (Day/Week/Month, All/Active/Left).
segmented.behavior: Click a segment to select it; exactly one segment is always selected. It switches the view or filters data immediately, no confirm button needed.
segmented.avoid: Navigating between pages — use Tabs. Toggling one independent state — use Switch.
segmented.when3: Picking one of 2–5 mutually exclusive modes
segmented.do1: Use it for 2–5 short, mutually exclusive items that need to be visible all at once.
segmented.do2: Give each segment a clear descriptive label so viewers instantly know what they're choosing.
segmented.dont1: Use it to navigate pages — that's Tabs' job, not Segmented's.
segmented.dont2: Use it for a single on/off state — use Switch instead.
segmented.exBasicD: A row of text labels to quickly switch the report view. Use it when text alone is clear enough, e.g. Day/Week/Month/Year time frames.
segmented.exIconD: Each segment has an icon and a label to switch between staff-list views. Icons help recognition when there are several options.
segmented.exIconOnlyD: Hide labels and show only icons to save space when the toolbar is tight. Good for a display-mode toggle (grid/list) on a toolbar.
segmented.exFillD: The segments stretch evenly to fill the container's width. Use it when Segmented sits in a fixed-width column or card.
segmented.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for dense UI (table filters), medium for most cases, large for areas that need to stand out.
segmented.exDisabledD: One item is disabled individually when that mode isn't available yet. Viewers still see the option but can't select it.
segmented.title: Segmented

slider.desc: Drag to pick a value or a range within a given span — salary level, percentage, age.
slider.purpose: Let users quickly pick a value level (or a range) by dragging the handle.
slider.behavior: Drag the handle to change the value; it moves smoothly by the step. Great for estimating, but not for numbers that must be exact.
slider.avoid: Needing an exact number — use Number Input.
slider.when2: Filtering by expected salary range, age range
slider.do1: Always give the slider a clear label so users know which value they're adjusting.
slider.do2: Show the value with a meaningful unit ("15 million", "75%") instead of a bare number.
slider.do3: Place marks at key positions so users can align quickly.
slider.dont1: Use a slider for a field that needs an absolutely exact number — use Number Input.
slider.dont2: Set the step so large that only a few positions remain — use Segmented or Radio instead.
slider.exBasicD: A single handle picks one value within a range. Use it for completion level, priority, percentage — where the value is relative.
slider.exRangeD: Two handles pick a range with a lower and upper bound. Good for filtering an expected salary range or candidate age range in recruitment.
slider.exMarksD: Place labeled marks at fixed positions so users can align quickly. Use it for a tiered proposed-salary scale.
slider.exStepD: A large step with dot marks so only preset stops can be picked. Good for a competency rating scale from 1 to 5.
slider.title: Slider

rate.desc: Pick a number of stars to quickly score a level or competency, on a 1–5 scale.
rate.purpose: Let users quickly score a criterion with visual stars (1–5).
rate.behavior: Click a star to set the level; click the current star again to reset to 0. Half stars can be enabled when more detail is needed.
rate.avoid: Data that isn't a ranking, or a scale that's too wide (0–100) — use Number Input.
rate.do1: Spell out what each star means (1 = Needs improvement … 5 = Excellent) to keep scoring consistent.
rate.do2: When showing an aggregated average, set it to read-only to avoid accidental edits.
rate.dont1: Use it for data that isn't a scale, or when an exact number is needed.
rate.exPerfD: A 5-star scale for one employee-performance criterion, e.g. work attitude or professional skills in a review cycle.
rate.exHalfD: Enable half stars when you need finer scoring than whole stars — useful to distinguish close levels like 3.5 and 4.
rate.exReadonlyD: An average score aggregated from several reviewers, shown read-only for viewing but not editing.
rate.exLabelD: A text label next to the stars helps reviewers understand what each level means, keeping ratings consistent across managers.
rate.title: Rate

select.desc: Pick one item from a long list without taking up much space; includes search and quick clear.
select.ovHelp: Type to filter the list quickly
select.purpose: Let users pick one item from a long list (department, job title, province) while saving space.
select.behavior: Click to open the list, type to filter, pick one item. A clear button resets it. When invalid, the border turns red with a message below.
select.avoid: Only 2–3 options that should all be visible at once — use Radio instead.
select.when1: Picking from a long list (department, job title, province)
select.when2: Screen space needs to be saved
select.when3: A list with many items needs type-to-filter
select.do1: Long lists (more than 7 items) should enable a search box for quick selection.
select.do2: Split a long list into titled groups for easier scanning (by division, by region).
select.do3: When invalid, state the reason clearly ("Please select a department") instead of just a red border.
select.dont1: Cramming hundreds of items into one flat list with no search or grouping.
select.exClearD: A clear button resets the selection to empty in one click. Handy when a filter needs a quick deselect without reopening the list.
select.exGroupD: The list is split into titled groups for easier scanning when there are many items — for example grouping job titles by department division.
select.exStateD: Error and warning states with a message help users know what to fix; once a valid choice is made, a short confirmation reassures them.
select.branchHelp: This branch is about to be discontinued
select.title: Select

autocomplete.desc: A free-text input with suggestions that appear as you type — a good fit when the option list is too long to show in full.
autocomplete.ovHelp: Type a name to see suggestions
autocomplete.purpose: Let users quickly pick an item from a large or frequently changing list by typing and choosing from suggestions.
autocomplete.behavior: Suggestions filter down by the characters typed. Users can still enter a value outside the suggestions. Picking a suggestion fills it into the field.
autocomplete.avoid: Short, fixed lists — use Select so users can see all options.
autocomplete.when1: The option list is too long to show in full
autocomplete.when2: A search box needs suggestions based on typed characters
autocomplete.when3: Quickly entering frequently used values (employee name, department)
autocomplete.do1: Set a placeholder that says what can be searched ("Search by name or employee ID").
autocomplete.do2: Show suggestions right when the field is focused, if there are recent items worth suggesting first.
autocomplete.do3: When several autocomplete fields sit side by side, give each a clear label to tell them apart.
autocomplete.dont1: Using it for short, fixed lists — Select is more discoverable.
autocomplete.dont2: Using it to pick multiple items at once — that is the job of a token input (Tokenizer).
autocomplete.exSearchD: A search field with employee-name suggestions that appear as you type. Use it for lookup bars where the list of people is too long to show in full.
autocomplete.exLimitD: Show at most three suggestions to stay compact — a good fit for very large data, avoiding a long dropdown that covers the screen.
autocomplete.exHelperD: A small description line under the label guides how to search — stating whether it matches by name or by code.
autocomplete.exErrorD: A red border with an error line when the value is invalid — telling users they must pick a valid employee from the list.
autocomplete.errPick: Please choose an employee from the list
autocomplete.title: AutoComplete

cascader.desc: Pick one value across several sequential levels: Unit › Department › Team, or Province › District › Ward.
cascader.purpose: Let users pick an item deep inside a multi-level hierarchy tree instead of scrolling one long flat list.
cascader.behavior: Selecting a parent level opens the next child level. The final result is a full path (e.g. South Region › HCM Branch › HR Department). A search box can be enabled to jump straight to the target item.
cascader.avoid: Flat lists with no hierarchy — use Select to keep it compact.
cascader.when1: Picking a unit in the org chart (Unit › Department › Team)
cascader.when2: Picking an administrative address (Province › District › Ward)
cascader.when3: Picking an item deep inside a multi-level classification tree
cascader.do1: Use it for real trees: org charts, administrative units (Province › District › Ward).
cascader.do2: Set a placeholder that names the first level to pick ("Select a unit").
cascader.do3: Enable search when the tree is deep or has many branches so users need not click level by level.
cascader.dont1: Forcing inherently flat data into a tree shape just to look hierarchical.
cascader.exOrgD: Pick a workplace by company chart: Unit › Department › Team. The result is a full path, so it is clear which branch the employee belongs to.
cascader.exAreaD: Pick an address by administrative unit: Province › District › Ward. Enable search to type a ward name directly instead of clicking each level in turn.
cascader.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for table filters, medium for most forms, large for a single prominent field on a page.
cascader.exStateD: Error, warning and valid. Red border when a required unit is not selected, yellow when a recheck is needed, green to confirm a correct choice.
cascader.title: Cascader

treeSelect.desc: Pick one or more nodes in a hierarchy tree: departments, units, job-title groups.
treeSelect.purpose: Let users pick a node in a hierarchy tree — usually a department/unit in the org chart.
treeSelect.behavior: Open the tree, type to search, then pick a node. Enable multi-select to tick several branches at once; a clear button quickly deselects.
treeSelect.avoid: Flat lists with no hierarchy — Select is more compact.
treeSelect.when1: Picking a department/unit in the org chart
treeSelect.when2: Picking several branches at once (job-title groups, regions)
treeSelect.when3: A required field that must be picked from a hierarchy structure
treeSelect.do1: Enable search when the tree is large and multi-level so users need not expand each branch.
treeSelect.do2: Keep the root branch expanded so the org structure is visible at a glance.
treeSelect.do3: On error, state what is wrong ("No department selected") instead of just a red border.
treeSelect.dont1: Using a tree for a flat list with no parent–child levels.
treeSelect.exDeptD: Pick a unit in the org tree. The root branch is expanded, with a search box to jump quickly to the target department.
treeSelect.exMultiD: Enable multi-select to tick several branches at once — for example choosing the job-title groups a policy applies to. Each choice appears as a removable tag.
treeSelect.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for dense table filters, medium for most forms, large for a single prominent field on a page.
treeSelect.exStateD: Error, warning and valid. Red border signals a required field not selected, yellow prompts a recheck, green confirms a valid choice.
treeSelect.title: Tree Select

mentions.desc: An input that lets you type @ to mention/tag a person right inside a note or comment.
mentions.purpose: Allow mentioning/tagging others right inside the content being typed (notes, comments, work discussions).
mentions.behavior: Typing @ shows a list of people to pick; once chosen, the name is inserted into the sentence. You can type it repeatedly to mention several people.
mentions.avoid: Ordinary information inputs that need not tag anyone — use Input or Textarea.
mentions.when1: Comments and work discussions that mention people by name
mentions.when2: Notes that need to tag the person in charge or an approver
mentions.when3: Reviews and minutes that need to pull the right people into the loop
mentions.do1: Use it in comments and notes that need to tag the person in charge or an approver so they get notified.
mentions.do2: Provide a ready list of suggestions of relevant people for quick selection, avoiding mistyped names.
mentions.dont1: Using it in place of a plain input when the content need not mention anyone.
mentions.exBasicD: Type @ in a note to mention a colleague. Use it in work discussions when you want to pull the right person in.
mentions.basicPh: Example: @an please help approve this request
mentions.exMixD: Type @ to mention a person, type # to mention a department. Useful when you need to notify both an individual and a group in one sentence.
mentions.mixPh: Example: @an and #nhansu please take a look
mentions.exLongD: A tall multi-line field for long notes with mentions. Use it for minutes and appraisal reviews where you need to write a lot and tag relevant people.
mentions.longPh: Enter a review… type @ to mention relevant people
mentions.exReadonlyD: A locked (non-editable) state when redisplaying saved content — for example reviewing an old comment in the approval history.
mentions.title: Mentions

transfer.desc: Move items back and forth between two lists — for example assigning employees to a project team.
transfer.purpose: Let users pick multiple items by moving them from the left list to the right and back.
transfer.behavior: Tick a few items, then click the arrow to move them to the other column. Both columns always clearly show which are unassigned and which are assigned.
transfer.avoid: Picking just a few simple items — use a multi-select Select to keep it compact.
transfer.when1: Assigning employees to a project team
transfer.when3: Picking many items where the selected state must be clearly visible
transfer.do1: Give each column a clear title (Unassigned / Assigned) so the move direction is obvious.
transfer.do2: Enable the search box when the list is long (many employees, many permissions).
transfer.do3: Lock items that must not change (core members, default permissions).
transfer.dont1: Using it when only one value needs picking — it is too heavy.
transfer.exAssignT: Transfer — Assign employees to a team
transfer.exAssignD: Two columns moving back and forth: unassigned people on the left, people already in the project team on the right. Tick, then click the arrow to move.
transfer.exSearchD: Add a search box on each column to filter quickly by name — use it when the employee list is long and hard to scan manually.
transfer.exLockedD: A few items are locked (dimmed, cannot be ticked) — for example the team lead and core members must stay in the team and cannot be moved out.
transfer.exReadonlyD: Lock everything to view the team makeup without editing — for people who do not have assignment rights.
transfer.title: Transfer

datePicker.desc: Pick one exact date from a calendar: start date, date of birth, contract expiry date.
datePicker.ovHelp: Pick the date the employee starts work
datePicker.purpose: Let users pick one exact date from a calendar (date of birth, start date, expiry date) instead of typing it, which is prone to format errors.
datePicker.behavior: Click to open the calendar and pick a date, or type it directly. The date shows as dd/MM/yyyy. Dates outside the limits are dimmed and cannot be picked.
datePicker.avoid: Picking a whole from–to range — use Range Picker.
datePicker.when1: Picking one specific date (date of birth, start date)
datePicker.when2: The date must fall within a valid range (min/max)
datePicker.when3: A timestamp that also needs a time (clock-in time)
datePicker.do1: Always give a clear label and a description when needed, so users know which date they are picking.
datePicker.do2: Use date limits (min/max) to block invalid dates — for example a date of birth cannot be in the future.
datePicker.do3: Keep the familiar dd/MM/yyyy date format to avoid confusing the day with the month.
datePicker.dont1: Making users type a free-form date with no calendar support — it is error-prone and hard to validate.
datePicker.exDescD: A small description line under the label clarifies which date the field needs when the label alone is not enough — for example the official signing date on a contract.
datePicker.signHelp: The date both parties officially sign
datePicker.exFormatD: Pick with a time for timestamps that need an exact time (clock-in time), and three field sizes: small for dense filters, medium for forms, large for a prominent field.
datePicker.exMinMaxD: Only allow dates within the valid range. A date of birth cannot be in the future; a start date cannot be before today — the remaining dates are dimmed.
datePicker.exStateD: Error, warning and valid states with a message, telling users what is wrong with the chosen date and how to fix it — or confirming the date is valid, much clearer than just a border.
datePicker.expireHelp: Recheck — the date is in the past
datePicker.title: Date Picker

timePicker.desc: Pick a time of day for attendance and shifts: shift-in time, shift-out time, lunch break time.
timePicker.purpose: Let users pick a moment in the day (shift-in time, shift-out time, clock-in time).
timePicker.behavior: Pick the hour and minute from a list; it shows 24-hour (HH:mm) by default. The value is saved as soon as it is picked.
timePicker.avoid: Needing to pick both a date and a time — use a separate Date Picker.
timePicker.when1: Picking shift-in / shift-out time in an attendance form
timePicker.when2: Setting a lunch break or overtime time
timePicker.when3: Setting a reminder time during the day
timePicker.do1: Use the 24-hour (HH:mm) format for attendance work to avoid AM/PM confusion.
timePicker.do2: Set a minute step that matches the work schedule (5 or 15 minutes) for fast, low-error selection.
timePicker.do3: When the time is invalid, state the reason clearly ("Shift-out time must be after shift-in time") instead of just a red border.
timePicker.dont1: Making users type a free-form, unvalidated time — it is prone to format errors.
timePicker.exBasicD: A standard 24-hour (HH:mm) time field. Use it for most shift-in and shift-out time fields in attendance forms.
timePicker.exFormatD: A 12-hour style with AM/PM, a 24-hour style, and a style with seconds. Use 24-hour for internal attendance, 12-hour when reporting to people used to reading AM/PM.
timePicker.exStepD: The minute list jumps by a fixed step (5 or 15 minutes) instead of every minute. It speeds up picking attendance times for fixed shifts.
timePicker.exStateD: Normal, error, warning, valid and non-editable states. Use error/warning to flag abnormal attendance times, green when the time is valid; lock the field when the time is recorded by the system.
timePicker.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for data-dense attendance tables, medium for regular forms, large for an entry page with one prominent field.
timePicker.title: Time Picker

rangePicker.desc: Let users pick a time span — from date to date — in the same calendar: leave periods, payroll periods, report filter ranges.
rangePicker.ovHelp: Pick a start date and an end date
rangePicker.purpose: Let users pick a time span (from date – to date) in one go, on the same calendar.
rangePicker.behavior: Pick the start date then the end date on the same calendar; the selected span is highlighted. You can type directly into the date field when you already know the dates. Dates outside the valid range are dimmed and cannot be picked.
rangePicker.avoid: Needing only a single date — use Date Picker.
rangePicker.when2: Filtering reports by date range (payroll period, attendance period)
rangePicker.when3: Setting a time span for on-call shifts or events
rangePicker.do1: Always give a clear label stating what the date range is for (leave period, payroll period, filter range).
rangePicker.do2: Block invalid dates with disabledDate — for example not allowing past dates when requesting leave.
rangePicker.do3: On error, state what is wrong ("The end date must be after the start date") instead of just a red border.
rangePicker.dont1: Using two separate date fields for from – to — it is easy to pick them in reverse and hard to see the total span length.
rangePicker.dont2: Making users rely on the calendar alone — allowing direct typing is faster when they already know the dates.
rangePicker.exLeaveD: Pick a leave date range on the same calendar. Block past dates with disabledDate so leave cannot be requested for a day that has passed.
rangePicker.exTimeD: Enable showTime to pick both date and time — use it for on-call shifts, half-day leave, or spans measured in work hours.
rangePicker.shiftHelp: Pick the start – end date and time
rangePicker.exStateD: Error, warning and valid states with a message. Tell users where the date range is wrong and how to fix it; a green border confirms the range is valid.
rangePicker.errRange: The end date must be after the start date
rangePicker.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for dense UI (report table filters), medium for most forms, large for a single prominent field on a page.
rangePicker.title: Range Picker

upload.desc: Let users choose or drag-and-drop files and images to attach to a record.
upload.purpose: Let users attach documents and images (records, supporting documents, avatars).
upload.behavior: Click the choose-file button or drag-and-drop into the upload area; chosen files appear as a list, and each can be removed.
upload.avoid: Entering text data — use the corresponding input fields.
upload.when3: Submitting a multi-file record set with a limit
upload.do1: Always state the allowed format and size so users choose the right file.
upload.do2: Set a count limit when allowing multiple files — to avoid uploading too many by mistake.
upload.do3: Use a drag-and-drop area when there is room — it is a familiar way to upload files.
upload.dont1: Allowing any format without control, with no upfront maximum size.
upload.exBtnD: A button to choose one file with the allowed formats. Use it for a standard record-attachment field in a form — contracts, decisions.
upload.exDragD: A large area that lets you drag files from your computer and drop them, or click to choose. Use it when the screen has room and several documents need uploading at once.
upload.dragText: Drag and drop files here or click to choose
upload.exAvatarD: A picture-card list that shows the uploaded thumbnail right away. Use it for employee avatars or a set of document images with previews.
upload.exLimitD: Accept only the right format and up to 3 files. Constraining format and count helps avoid uploading the wrong file or too many.
upload.title: Upload

colorPicker.desc: Let users pick a color to assign to a label, group or project, helping tell them apart quickly by eye.
colorPicker.purpose: Let users pick a color to assign to a label, group or project — helping quick recognition by color.
colorPicker.behavior: Click the color swatch to open the picker; once chosen, the small swatch shows the selected color, with the color code if enabled.
colorPicker.avoid: Allowing arbitrary colors where the interface must stay consistent — limit choices to a predefined palette.
colorPicker.when1: Assigning colors to leave types, statuses, categories
colorPicker.when2: Telling group/project labels apart by color
colorPicker.when3: Picking colors from a predefined palette to keep consistency
colorPicker.do1: Provide a predefined palette so everyone picks consistently, without drifting from the brand tone.
colorPicker.do2: Enable show color code when exact matching is needed (for example matching a color to a printed document).
colorPicker.do3: Use it for meaningful color assignment: leave types, statuses, group/project labels.
colorPicker.dont1: Allowing free interface color changes that break consistency.
colorPicker.exLabelD: Pick a color to assign to a group or project label, helping tell them apart quickly in a list. This is the most basic use.
colorPicker.exPresetD: Provide suggested colors so everyone picks quickly and consistently, avoiding a different tone per person. A good fit when assigning colors by a brand identity.
colorPicker.exCodeD: Enable showing the color code next to the swatch for exact matching; turn it off when you only need to see the color, for a cleaner look.
colorPicker.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for dense table rows, medium for regular forms, large when the color is a prominent choice on the screen.
colorPicker.title: Color Picker

formField.desc: A wrapper around an input: adds a label, a required/optional marker, a description line and an error message for the control inside.
formField.ovHelp: Used to receive notifications and payslips
formField.purpose: Wrap a control to add a label, description, required/optional marker and error message that the control itself lacks.
formField.behavior: The label always shows above. The description sits between the label and the input. On error, a red line appears below the field and replaces the description line.
formField.avoid: Wrapping controls that already have their own label/description — the label would appear twice.
formField.when1: Wrapping a custom control or a native control that has no label/description
formField.when2: Needing to mark a field as required or optional
formField.when3: Needing to show a validation error message below the input
formField.do1: Always give a label so users and screen readers know what the field is for.
formField.do2: Use the description to spell out the format or constraint ("At least 8 characters", "A confirmation link will be sent to this email").
formField.do3: Mark fields required when they must be filled and optional when they can be skipped — so users know upfront.
formField.dont1: Marking a single field as both required and optional — the two markers are mutually exclusive.
formField.dont2: Hiding the label with no other way for users to understand what the field is for.
formField.exDescD: A small description line under the label to explain the format, constraint or what the data will be used for — such as 'At least 8 characters' or 'A confirmation link will be sent'.
formField.pwHelp: At least 8 characters, with letters and numbers
formField.personalEmailHelp: A confirmation link will be sent to this address
formField.exReqD: Required and optional markers side by side. Use required for fields that must be filled, optional for fields that can be skipped, so users know upfront.
formField.exStateD: Error, warning and valid states with a message. Error for wrong data, warning for cases that need attention such as an existing code, valid when the input is correct.
formField.codeHelp: This code already exists, please recheck
formField.exControlsD: The same field wrapper around every control type: input, select, date picker, switch, textarea — labels and descriptions always stay aligned.
formField.notifyHelp: Turn on to receive reminders and approvals by email
formField.title: Form Field

echart.desc: Interactive charts built on Apache ECharts, auto-themed from design tokens (palette, typography, axes, grid, Light/Dark). Pass an ECharts config and the component handles colors and resizing.
echart.purpose: Visualize multi-point / multi-series data to reveal trends, comparisons and composition — more capable than a mini widget.
echart.behavior: Pass an option per the ECharts docs (series/xAxis/yAxis…); no need to set colors — the component pulls from the token palette and follows Light/Dark automatically. Includes tooltip, legend, zoom and responsive resizing.
echart.avoid: A single number or tiny trend line — use a Stat Card / Sparkline instead (lightweight, no full chart library).
echart.when1: Trend reports across many months and series
echart.when2: Comparing departments / branches by a metric
echart.when3: A chart block on a dashboard or report page
echart.do1: Let the component color series from tokens — don't hardcode colors in the option (keeps the whole system consistent).
echart.do2: Place the chart in a card with a title and filters to form a complete dashboard block.
echart.dont1: Cram too many series into one chart — split them or let users toggle series via the legend.
echart.exLineD: Trends over time, multiple series. A soft-filled area highlights the primary series. Good for headcount or monthly attendance.
echart.exBarD: Compare values across groups; stacked bars show the composition within each group (official / probation by department).
echart.exPieD: Composition of a single total. The donut leaves the center free to place the total.
echart.exComboD: Two units on one frame: bars = counts (left axis), line = percentage (right axis). Tells the 'volume vs performance' story.
echart.exCardD: A chart inside a titled card — a compact dashboard block that groups charts by context.
echart.title: Chart library

competencyRadar.desc: A radar chart comparing current competencies against a role's requirements — one shape reveals which criteria fall short (the GAP), supporting appraisals and development plans.
competencyRadar.purpose: Quickly see the GAP between an employee's actual competencies and the role standard, across many criteria at once.
competencyRadar.behavior: Each axis is a competency criterion; two areas overlap (Current / Required). Where the 'Current' area sinks inside 'Required' is exactly what needs training.
competencyRadar.avoid: Too many criteria (>8 axes) gets cluttered; for a single criterion — use a progress bar.
competencyRadar.when3: Matching candidates against a role's competency framework
competencyRadar.do1: Keep 5–7 criteria on the same scale so the shape stays balanced and the GAP is easy to read.
competencyRadar.do2: Always include the 'Required' series as a baseline — a radar alone can't tell short from sufficient.
competencyRadar.dont1: Mixing several people into one radar — one radar per employee/role.
competencyRadar.exGapD: The bold area = current competencies, the light area = role requirements. Look at the dips to see what to develop.
competencyRadar.exCardD: Place it in an employee profile card beside their details — a compact competency-assessment block.
competencyRadar.title: Competency radar (GAP)

recruitmentFunnel.desc: A funnel chart shows how many candidates remain at each recruitment step — a stage that narrows sharply is where the most drop-off happens and needs review.
recruitmentFunnel.purpose: See the conversion rate between recruitment steps and spot the 'bottleneck' stage that loses candidates.
recruitmentFunnel.behavior: Each stage is as wide as its count; labels show the number + % relative to the first stage. A sudden narrowing = low conversion.
recruitmentFunnel.avoid: Steps that don't narrow in order — a funnel is only valid when numbers decrease step by step.
recruitmentFunnel.when2: Finding the bottleneck step in the process
recruitmentFunnel.do1: Name stages after your real process; keep 4–6 stages.
recruitmentFunnel.do2: Include a detailed data table alongside when exact per-stage figures are needed.
recruitmentFunnel.dont1: Using a funnel for data without a 'progressive filtering' relationship — use a plain bar chart.
recruitmentFunnel.exProcessD: Applied → Screening → Interview → Offer → Hired. Look at the narrow stages to see where candidates are lost.
recruitmentFunnel.exCardD: Place it in a titled card — a 'recruitment effectiveness' block for the HR dashboard.
recruitmentFunnel.title: Recruitment funnel

kpiGauge.desc: A gauge measuring progress toward a target: the arc fills by % completed and changes color by level (red low, amber fair, green met). One glance shows how far the goal is.
kpiGauge.purpose: Represent ONE progress ratio (0–100%) visually, with color thresholds for a quick alert.
kpiGauge.behavior: The arc fills by value; color changes by level (red <50, amber <80, green ≥80). A large number in the center, label below.
kpiGauge.avoid: Many metrics at once — one ratio per gauge; to compare many items use a Bar List.
kpiGauge.do1: Use it for ratios with a clear 'target' (KPI, progress, attendance rate).
kpiGauge.do2: Line up several gauges in a row for different teams/departments.
kpiGauge.dont1: Using it for absolute numbers with no ceiling — use a Stat Card.
kpiGauge.exLevelsD: The same gauge, arc color changing by level attained: low (red), fair (amber), met (green).
kpiGauge.exCardD: Place it in a titled card for a 'target completion' block on the dashboard.
kpiGauge.title: KPI gauge

attendanceHeatmap.desc: An hour × day heatmap: the darker a cell, the more people present / active. Instantly reveals peak hours, empty days and heavily loaded shifts.
attendanceHeatmap.purpose: Spot time-based patterns (peak hours, empty days) that a data table hides — through shading intensity.
attendanceHeatmap.behavior: Horizontal axis = hour/shift, vertical axis = day; cell color follows density (color scale below). Hover to see the exact number.
attendanceHeatmap.avoid: Data that is too sparse (many empty cells) — a heatmap only looks good when the matrix is relatively full.
attendanceHeatmap.when2: Comparing attendance load across days of the week
attendanceHeatmap.when3: Seeing which shift/time slot is busiest
attendanceHeatmap.do1: Keep a single-hue scale (light → dark) so density is easy to compare; note the unit.
attendanceHeatmap.do2: Include the number in the tooltip for those who need the exact figure.
attendanceHeatmap.dont1: Using many vivid colors for cells — it destroys density comparison.
attendanceHeatmap.exWeekD: Hour of day × day of week. Dark cells = many badge scans, clearly showing peak check-in/out hours.
attendanceHeatmap.exCardD: Place it in a card for an attendance-analysis block on the dashboard.
attendanceHeatmap.title: Attendance heatmap

chartTable.desc: Pair a chart with a data table in one block: the chart gives a quick sense, the table gives exact figures — a familiar report-page pattern.
chartTable.purpose: Answer both 'how does the overall look' (chart) and 'what's the exact number' (table) in one block.
chartTable.behavior: The chart and table share one data source. Stack vertically (chart above, table below) when narrow; side by side (chart left, table right) when wide. Same token palette, so series colors match.
chartTable.avoid: Repeating identical data without adding value — only pair them when the table adds detail the chart can't fully show.
chartTable.when2: An "overview + detail" block on the dashboard
chartTable.when3: Exporting reports that need both visuals and numbers
chartTable.do1: Use one shared data source for both chart and table so numbers never diverge.
