dateCell.dont2: Cramming the date, time and a long note into one secondary line — the secondary line should be one very short note.
dateCell.exDateD: The default mode. Fits hire dates, contract signing dates, expiry dates — where you only need the date, not the time.
dateCell.exDatetimeD: Shows both date and time in one cell. Use it for moments that need minute precision — when a request was sent, approved, or a profile updated.
dateCell.exTimeD: Shows just hour:minute, dropping the date. Fits an intraday timesheet — clock-in, clock-out — when the date is already clear in the table title or another column.
dateCell.exSubD: Add a short note right below the timestamp, e.g. 'yesterday' or '3 days ago'. Note: this text is composed and passed in by whoever prepares the data; the cell doesn't compute it.
dateCell.when1: The "Hire date", "Contract signing date", "Expiry date" columns
dateCell.when2: Timesheet: clock-in / clock-out within a day
dateCell.when3: The moment a request was sent, approved, or last updated
dateCell.title: Date Cell

actionCell.desc: Gathers the actions at the end of a table row — View, Edit, Delete… — into a compact cluster of icon buttons, always in the last column.
actionCell.purpose: Let users act quickly on exactly one table row: view details, edit, delete, download… right at the end of that row.
actionCell.behavior: Each action is a small icon button. When the number of actions exceeds the allowed limit, the overflow collapses into a three-dots button to open later, keeping the last column tidy. The Delete button (and other dangerous actions) turns red on hover as a warning. Unavailable actions are dimmed and unclickable. Clicking a button affects only that row, without triggering the whole row.
actionCell.avoid: Putting table-wide actions (Add, Export to Excel, Filter) here — those belong in the toolbar above the table, not in each row.
actionCell.do1: Put the most-used actions (View, Edit) first; place rarely used ones later or fold them into the three dots.
actionCell.do2: Always name each button clearly (View, Edit, Delete) so a tooltip shows on hover and screen-reader users hear what it does.
actionCell.do3: Use red only for genuinely dangerous actions like Delete, so users pause a beat before clicking.
actionCell.dont1: Cramming too many buttons into one row and cluttering the last column — keep a few key actions and move the rest into the three dots.
actionCell.dont2: Fully hiding an action the user isn't permitted to use — consider dimming (disabling) it if you still want to show it exists.
actionCell.exStdD: The most common layout for an employee list table: View profile, Edit details, Delete. The Delete button turns red on hover because it's an irreversible action.
actionCell.exMoreT: Collapse when there are many actions
actionCell.exMoreD: When a row has many actions, set a limit on visible buttons — here 2 — and the rest fold into the three-dots button. The last column stays tidy; users click the three dots to see the remaining actions.
actionCell.exDisabledD: An unavailable action — due to missing permission or unmet conditions — still shows but dimmed and unclickable. Here the record is locked, so Delete isn't allowed.
actionCell.exDocT: An action set for a document record
actionCell.exDocD: The same action cell reused for a record/document table with different actions: View, Download, Duplicate, Delete. Pick the actions that fit each table's context.
actionCell.rowMore: Show 2 buttons · overflow folds into the three dots
actionCell.when1: The last column of employee, record and contract list tables
actionCell.when2: Anywhere you need quick per-row actions: view, edit, delete
actionCell.when3: Tables with many actions that need collapsing into one cluster
actionCell.title: Action Cell

buttonGroup.desc: Group several related action buttons into one seamless cluster — shared border, rounded corners at each end.
buttonGroup.purpose: Group related actions or modes into one cluster so users see they belong together.
buttonGroup.behavior: Buttons sit flush with a shared border; the first is rounded on the left, the last on the right. Same size and style so they read as one block.
buttonGroup.avoid: Unrelated buttons — use spacing (Space) instead of a flush cluster.
buttonGroup.when2: A cluster of related actions on a toolbar
buttonGroup.do1: Keep all buttons the same style and size so the cluster reads as one block.
buttonGroup.do2: Use for actions of the same kind or for switching views.
buttonGroup.dont1: Mixing styles (primary + dashed + text) in one cluster — visually noisy.
buttonGroup.exBasicD: Three related actions combined into one seamless control. Keep the same style so it reads as one block.
buttonGroup.exViewD: An icon-only cluster to change how a list is displayed: grid, list, columns.
buttonGroup.exVertD: A vertically stacked cluster for a side toolbar or a narrow action list.
buttonGroup.exBlockD: block: each button is equal and fills the full width — good for a full-width Previous/Next navigation bar.
buttonGroup.title: Button Group

iconButton.desc: A compact square button with only an icon — for action bars where space is tight. Always include a label for screen readers.
iconButton.purpose: Trigger an action with just an icon when the context is clear enough and space must be saved.
iconButton.behavior: A square, icon-only button. An ariaLabel is REQUIRED so screen readers announce its function; add a tooltip for sighted users.
iconButton.avoid: Important or rare actions where the icon is not clear enough — use a button with text.
iconButton.when2: Frequently repeated actions with familiar icons
iconButton.when3: Tight space (inside a table row, a toolbar)
iconButton.do1: Always set an ariaLabel and a tooltip describing the action (an icon alone is easy to misread).
iconButton.do2: Use for common actions with familiar icons (edit, delete, download, share).
iconButton.dont1: Placing a dangerous icon-only action without confirmation — easy to click by mistake.
iconButton.exBarD: A compact row of text-style icon buttons for a toolbar — edit, copy, download, share, delete.
iconButton.exLoadingD: Click to run a task; the button shows a spinner while processing (async feedback).
iconButton.exTooltipD: Hovering the button shows a note explaining the action — compensating for the icon alone.
iconButton.exShapeD: Square, rounded or circular; three sizes small/medium/large for different UI densities.
iconButton.title: Icon Button

toggleButton.desc: A stateful button — click to turn on, click again to turn off. Use it for switching views or a formatting bar.
toggleButton.purpose: Represent a two-state choice (on/off) while keeping the shape of a button.
toggleButton.behavior: On = solid background (primary), off = normal border. It exposes aria-pressed. Combine several toggles into a group for single-select (switching modes) or multi-select (formatting).
toggleButton.avoid: Turning a setting on/off inside a form — a Switch is clearer.
toggleButton.do1: Use when the on/off state maps to an immediate action (bold, alignment, view mode).
toggleButton.do2: Group single-select to replace a mode switcher; multi-select for a formatting bar.
toggleButton.dont1: Using it instead of a Switch for a persistent setting (turn on email notifications…) — a Switch is clearer.
toggleButton.exBasicD: A single stateful button: click to turn on, click again to turn off. Solid background when on.
toggleButton.exSingleD: A single-select toggle cluster as a view switcher: grid / list / columns (always exactly one on).
toggleButton.exMultiD: A cluster of independent toggles as a text formatting bar: bold, italic, underline (several on at once).
toggleButton.exIconT: Toggle Button — Icon changes when on
toggleButton.exIconD: The icon changes from outline to filled when on — for example a Favorite button (empty star → gold star).
toggleButton.title: Toggle Button

floatButton.desc: A round button floating fixed in the screen corner for a global action, always within reach no matter how far you scroll.
floatButton.purpose: Bring a global action to the screen corner so users can always reach it (quick add, back to top, open support).
floatButton.behavior: Always visible in the screen corner no matter how far you scroll. Click to run the action; a group expands into child buttons on click or hover.
floatButton.avoid: Cramming many of a form's business actions into a float button — it hides content and causes clutter.
floatButton.when1: A list page needing an "add new" button always within reach
floatButton.when2: A long scroll needing a "back to top" button
floatButton.when3: A support/inbox button that stays visible
floatButton.do1: Keep only one float-button cluster per screen, for the most important action.
floatButton.do2: Always use a clear icon; add a short description when the icon is not clear enough.
floatButton.do3: Gather related actions into one expanding group instead of stacking several separate buttons.
floatButton.dont1: Cramming a form's main buttons (Save, Submit) into a float button.
floatButton.exAddD: A round float button at the bottom-right for the page's main action — usually creating a new record. The primary color makes it stand out; a secondary button takes users to the top of a long list.
floatButton.exGroupD: Gather several related actions under one parent button; click or hover to expand the options. Use it when a screen needs a few quick actions without stacking separate buttons in the corner.
floatButton.rowGroup: Click the plus to expand — Add · Import · Export
floatButton.exBadgeD: A count/dot badge flags something that needs attention (new messages, unread notifications); a short description under the icon says what the button does. Use for a support button or an always-visible inbox.
floatButton.title: Float Button

gridGrouped.desc: A table that groups rows by one column's value (group by): each group has a header and a total row.
gridGrouped.purpose: View data grouped by a criterion (department, status, month…) with a total per group.
gridGrouped.behavior: Each group is a header with a total row (count/sum). Cells use Table Cells components: user cell, skill tags, amount, status.
gridGrouped.avoid: Flat data that needs no grouping — use a regular Data Grid.
gridGrouped.when2: Summaries with a total/count per group
gridGrouped.do1: Group by a column with FEW distinct values (department, status).
gridGrouped.do2: Show a total/count per group for a quick read.
gridGrouped.dont1: Grouping by a high-cardinality column (employee ID) — every group becomes a single row, which is meaningless.
gridGrouped.exD: Group employees by department; the group header shows name + headcount + total salary. Each row is a user cell (avatar + title + presence dot), skill tags, salary, status.
gridGrouped.title: Grouped Table

gridMasterDetail.desc: Each parent row can expand to show details/a sub-grid (a nested table) without leaving the page.
gridMasterDetail.openHint: Click the arrow at the start of a row to open the detail grid.
gridMasterDetail.purpose: View a summary record and its child details right in the same table (order → line items, employee → contracts…).
gridMasterDetail.behavior: Each parent row has an expand control; expanding shows a sub-grid below. The parent row uses Table Cells components: order cell, requester cell, amount, status.
gridMasterDetail.avoid: Details too large or with many actions — open a separate page/drawer.
gridMasterDetail.when2: A parent record with child items for a quick look
gridMasterDetail.do1: Use when the detail is short and can be scanned without leaving context.
gridMasterDetail.dont1: Nesting many levels of master-detail — confusing and hard to follow.
gridMasterDetail.exD: The parent row is a purchase order (order cell with icon + code, requester cell, total, approval status); it expands to a sub-grid of line items with line totals.
gridMasterDetail.title: Master-Detail

gridPivot.desc: A multi-dimensional cross-tab summary: rows × columns × measure, with row/column totals — like an Excel PivotTable.
gridPivot.mockNote: ⚠ Static mock. An interactive pivot (drag-drop dimensions, measures, drill-down) is not available in ng-zorro — roadmap: integrate a pivot library or build an SVG/table engine later.
gridPivot.purpose: Summarize one measure (headcount, salary, cost) crossed over 2+ dimensions (department × time).
gridPivot.behavior: Choose row/column dimensions + a measure → a cross-tab with row totals, column totals, and a grand total.
gridPivot.avoid: Only one dimension — use a Grouped Grid or a bar chart.
gridPivot.do1: Use for management reports: cost by department × month, headcount × level.
gridPivot.dont1: Too many dimensions/values — a huge, unreadable table; limit to 2–3 dimensions.
gridPivot.exD: Headcount by department (rows) and quarter (columns), with row/column/grand totals. Use for staffing reports and resource allocation.
gridPivot.title: Pivot Table

enterpriseGrid.desc: A table showing many rows of data in columns — the core component of HRM management screens.
enterpriseGrid.purpose: Present a list of records in columns to look up, sort, select, and process in bulk.
enterpriseGrid.behavior: Each row is a record; columns are fields. Click a column header to sort; check the box at the start of a row to select multiple rows. Cells can use Table Cells components: user, tags, progress, status, actions.
enterpriseGrid.avoid: A simple list with no columns — use a List. Hierarchical parent-child data — use a Tree List.
enterpriseGrid.when2: Management screens needing lookup, sorting, and bulk selection
enterpriseGrid.do1: Put important columns first; right-align numbers/amounts for easy comparison.
enterpriseGrid.do2: Use the prebuilt table cells (user cell, status cell, action cell) so each row scans quickly and consistently.
enterpriseGrid.dont1: Cramming in too many columns hurts readability — hide minor columns or allow horizontal scroll.
enterpriseGrid.exRecordT: Table — Single record (one row per column)
enterpriseGrid.exRecordD: variant='record': displays ONE record vertically — each column becomes a label | value row. Reuses the same Table Cells (user cell, two-line cell, tags cell, progress cell, status cell). Good for an employee/order detail page.
enterpriseGrid.exToolbarD: The bar above the table: title + record count on the left, a search box in the middle (auto-expands), action buttons on the right. Gathers all table actions in one place.
enterpriseGrid.exRichT: Table — Rich cells with Table Cells
enterpriseGrid.exRichD: The standard table: horizontal dividers between rows, no vertical column dividers. Columns plug in Table Cells directly: user cell, two-line cell, tags cell, progress cell, status cell, action cell.
enterpriseGrid.exSortD: Click a column header to sort ascending/descending. Enable it for columns worth comparing: employee name (A–Z) or KPI progress (numeric).
enterpriseGrid.exSelectD: A checkbox at the start of each row and a 'select all' box in the header — for bulk actions like exporting a list or assigning permissions. A partial selection → the header box shows a dash (indeterminate).
enterpriseGrid.exStripedD: Alternating row backgrounds help the eye track horizontally in tables with many rows and columns.
enterpriseGrid.exDividersD: Four divider styles per Astryx: rows (horizontal, default — easy to track by row), columns (vertical — compare by column), grid (both — spreadsheet-style lookup), none (clean — short tables with few rows). Row density is not configured here — change it globally in Config (the gear at the top-right).
enterpriseGrid.exTruncD: truncate: long text is cut with an ellipsis instead of wrapping — rows stay uniformly tall and scan fast. Hover a truncated cell to see the full content (tooltip). The column needs a width. wrap (default) allows line breaks.
enterpriseGrid.exInCardD: The table sits in a card with a title, flush: removes body padding — the table reaches the card's edges, header and rows run full width.
enterpriseGrid.title: Table

treeList.desc: Hierarchical parent-child data shown in a COLUMNED TABLE: each parent row expands/collapses, children are indented — like an org chart.
treeList.purpose: Present hierarchical data (an org chart, a category tree) WHILE still needing several attribute columns.
treeList.behavior: The first column is the tree (indentation + an expand/collapse arrow); the following columns are each node's attributes.
treeList.avoid: A plain tree with no attribute columns — use a Tree (Data Entry). Flat data — use a Data Grid.
treeList.when1: An org chart with figures in columns
treeList.do1: The first column is the tree; the following columns are the node's figures/attributes.
treeList.do2: Expand the first 1–2 levels to show the structure, leave deeper levels for users to open.
treeList.dont1: A tree too deep (>5 levels) in a table — hard to read; consider a dedicated page.
treeList.exD: Unit (tree) × Head × Headcount. Click the arrow to expand/collapse a division/department. Use for org structures and category trees with figures.
treeList.title: Tree List

divider.desc: A thin line that separates groups of unrelated content on the same screen.
divider.purpose: Visually separate groups of unrelated content: split an employee profile into sections, divide clusters on a toolbar.
divider.behavior: A thin line that can carry a title in the center or aligned left/right. A horizontal rule separates stacked blocks; a vertical rule separates items placed side by side.
divider.avoid: Overusing a rule on every line — prefer whitespace and layout to group content whenever possible.
divider.when1: Separating two groups of unrelated content in a profile/form
divider.when2: Adding a small heading between sections
divider.when3: Separating horizontal metrics or button clusters with a vertical rule
divider.do1: Use a thin rule between related sections; only use bold/dashed when you need a more prominent boundary.
divider.do2: Add a title to the rule when each section needs a visible group heading ("Contract", "Salary").
divider.dont1: Draw a divider between every line — use whitespace and layout to separate content instead.
divider.exHorizD: A plain horizontal rule separates two stacked content blocks. Use it between related sections in a profile or info card.
divider.exTextD: A rule with a group title in the center or aligned left/right. Use it when each section needs a visible section label.
divider.exVertD: A vertical rule separates horizontal metrics or items. Use it between stat cards or button clusters on a toolbar.
divider.exDashedD: A dashed rule for a light boundary, implying secondary content. Use it when you want a softer separation than a solid line.
divider.title: Divider

flex.desc: Arrange elements into rows or columns with even spacing.
flex.purpose: Quickly arrange elements side by side (buttons, cards, inputs) in a row or column, evenly spaced.
flex.behavior: Choose the direction (row/column), the gap between elements, and the alignment (start, center, space between). Elements can wrap to the next line when they run out of room.
flex.avoid: Multi-column grid layouts that need horizontal and vertical alignment — use Grid.
flex.when1: Laying out a group of buttons or cards in a row
flex.when2: Aligning to both ends: title on the left, actions on the right
flex.when3: Stacking info lines in a column
flex.do1: Use it for toolbars, button groups, card rows — where elements sit together in one strip.
flex.do2: Pick one consistent gap within the same group so it looks tidy.
flex.do3: Enable wrapping when the number of elements may exceed the screen width (filters, tags).
flex.dont1: Force a 12/24-column grid layout into Flex — rows will break when the screen shrinks.
flex.exJustifyD: Lay out horizontally and choose the alignment: start for button groups, center for balanced content, space between for a title with actions.
flex.exColumnD: Set the direction to column to stack elements — good for a list of info lines or a group of fields in a form.
flex.exWrapD: When there are more elements than the width allows, let them wrap instead of overflowing. Small, medium and large gaps change the breathing room between elements.
flex.title: Flex

space.desc: Set even spacing between small elements placed side by side, such as buttons or labels.
space.purpose: Create even spacing between elements in the same row (buttons, labels, cards) without hand-tuning each margin.
space.behavior: Automatically inserts equal gaps between child elements and wraps to the next line when it runs out of room.
space.avoid: Layouts with multiple regions or directions — use Flex or Grid.
space.when1: A group of buttons or cards placed side by side
space.when2: You need even spacing in a simple single direction
space.do1: Use it for a group of buttons or cards side by side in the same row.
space.do2: Keep one consistent gap for similar groups across the whole screen.
space.dont1: Using it for complex multi-column or multi-level layouts.
space.exHorizD: Lay out a group of buttons in a horizontal row with even spacing. Commonly used for action button clusters at the end of a form or on a toolbar.
space.exSizeD: Choose the gap width to match interface density: tight for dense button clusters, medium for most cases, wide when you need to separate groups for breathing room.
space.exVertD: Stack buttons in a vertical column with even spacing. Good for an action menu in a narrow card or a quick-pick panel.
space.title: Space

layoutGrid.desc: Divide the screen into columns to arrange dashboard and profile content; columns adapt to the screen width.
layoutGrid.purpose: Arrange content into equal columns for dashboards and employee profiles; columns wrap to the next line on narrow screens.
layoutGrid.behavior: The screen is divided into 24 parts; each cell takes the number of parts you set. On phones, cells stack into a single column for readability.
layoutGrid.avoid: Confusing it with a data table — this is a screen layout, not a place to list employees row by row.
layoutGrid.when2: Dashboards split into cells with a large overview cell
layoutGrid.when3: An employee card gallery that adapts on phones
layoutGrid.do1: Use responsive (xs/md/lg) for layouts that must adapt: 3 columns when wide, stacked when narrow.
layoutGrid.do2: Give important cells more span (overview cell, chart) to guide the viewer's eye.
layoutGrid.do3: Keep the gutter even between cells so the layout stays tidy and easy to read.
layoutGrid.dont1: Using a grid to display a row-by-row data list — use a Table.
layoutGrid.exEqualD: Split a row into equal cells for a balanced layout. Use it for 2–3 column profile forms or a row of equal-width stat cards on a dashboard.
layoutGrid.exGutterD: The gutter between cells determines the breathing room of the layout. Tight for data-dense grids, wide for overview cards that need room to breathe.
layoutGrid.exResponsiveD: The same card row: 3 columns on desktop, stacked into a single column on phones. Use it for an employee card gallery or stat cells that display well on any device.
layoutGrid.exSpanD: Give an important cell more span to make it stand out, or leave a margin with an offset to align content. Use it for dashboards with a large overview cell and a full-width summary row.
layoutGrid.title: Grid

affix.desc: Keep an element pinned in place as the user scrolls the page.
affix.purpose: Keep an important button or toolbar visible while the user scrolls a long page.
affix.behavior: When scrolling reaches its position, the element sticks to the top (or bottom) of the viewport; scrolling back returns it to its original spot.
affix.avoid: Pinning too many things at once — it hides content and confuses users.
affix.when1: A long page that needs to keep a filter bar or save button in view
affix.when2: A back-to-top button placed at the bottom of the screen
affix.do1: Pin a filter bar or save button on a long page so users can always act.
affix.do2: Leave a small offset so the element doesn't stick to the very edge of the screen.
affix.dont1: Pinning several large blocks at once, hiding the main content.
affix.exTopD: The button sticks to the top of the viewport when scrolling down, a small offset from the top edge. Use it for a primary action button or a toolbar that must stay visible.
affix.exBottomD: The button sticks to the bottom of the viewport instead of the top. Good for a back-to-top button or an action bar placed at the bottom of the screen.
affix.title: Affix

watermark.desc: Overlay a faint, repeating text or logo across a content area to reinforce security and deter screenshots or copying of documents.
watermark.purpose: Overlay a faint watermark on content to reinforce confidentiality and deter screenshots or leaks of sensitive documents.
watermark.behavior: A faint text or logo repeats behind the content, slightly rotated and sparse so it doesn't hinder reading. The watermark tracks the content area and scrolls with the page.
watermark.avoid: Making the watermark too dark or too dense so it hides the text — it only needs to be enough to signal 'confidential document'.
watermark.when1: Views for contracts, payslips, sensitive profiles
watermark.when3: You need to trace who viewed a document (name + date)
watermark.do1: Use it for views of contracts, payslips, candidate profiles — where you need to signal "do not share externally".
watermark.do2: Keep the watermark faint and sparse, just enough to read, prioritizing content.
watermark.do3: Combine the viewer's name + date so if a screenshot leaks out, the source can still be traced.
watermark.dont1: Overlaying a watermark so dark/dense that it makes the main content hard to read.
watermark.exMarkD: Overlay a faint 'CONFIDENTIAL' text on the profile content to signal that this is an internal document, not to be shared externally.
watermark.exMarkLine: Department: Human Resources — Salary and performance reviews are for authorized personnel only.
watermark.exMultiD: Combine the current viewer's name and access date into the watermark — if the document is captured and leaks out, you can still trace who viewed it and when.
watermark.exMultiLine: Gross income, deductions and net pay — personal information, do not share.
watermark.exLogoD: Use the company logo as a watermark for internally published documents, asserting the source while keeping the content readable.
watermark.exLogoLine: VNR internal document — please do not distribute outside the organization.
watermark.title: Watermark

appShell.desc: The outermost layout of the app: combines Side Nav, Top Nav and the page content area. It arranges itself based on which slots are present.
appShell.ovNote: Default: full Side Nav on the left (logo + bell + collapse + switch account + user block) · page content on the right — the user's eye goes straight to the screen.
appShell.purpose: The outermost frame that wraps every page: fixed navigation (side/top), with its own scrollable content area.
appShell.behavior: The [appSideNav] slot is full height on the left; [appTopNav] sits above the right area; the content is the remaining area (scrollable). The layout adjusts to whichever slots are present.
appShell.avoid: A static single-column page that doesn't need a navigation frame — no App Shell needed.
appShell.when1: The root frame wrapping every page of the app
appShell.when2: You need fixed navigation + a separately scrolling content area
appShell.when3: A large app combining side nav + top nav
appShell.do1: Make App Shell the root frame of every page; only the content area scrolls, nav stays fixed.
appShell.do2: Combine the right components Side Nav / Top Nav — App Shell only handles layout, it doesn't rebuild the nav.
appShell.dont1: Placing the logo in BOTH side nav and top nav when combined — duplicate branding, pick one place.
appShell.exSideD: Vertical navigation on the left (full Side Nav), content area on the right. A common layout for admin apps.
appShell.exTopD: Horizontal navigation on top, content below. Suits apps with flat navigation and few destinations.
appShell.exBothT: App Shell — Side Nav + Top Nav + Content
appShell.exBothD: Combined: full Side Nav on the left (full height) + Top Nav above the right area + content below. For large, feature-rich apps.
appShell.pageSub: Updated today · Where you place your prototype
appShell.title: App Shell

sideNav.desc: A vertical navigation bar that organizes the app's pages into groups, nested items and icons; with a user account block at the bottom.
sideNav.ovNote: Click an item to change page; the bell + account block (bottom) open a dropdown; the collapse button → icon rail: selected/hovered items become squares, the account block keeps just the avatar.
sideNav.purpose: Vertical navigation to organize the app's pages into groups, nested items and icons; the user account sits at the bottom.
sideNav.behavior: PRIMARY navigation when the app has ≥5 destinations or needs a hierarchy. The selected item stands out; sub-groups expand/collapse; it collapses into a square-icon rail; the account block is pinned to the bottom.
sideNav.avoid: An app with only 2–3 flat destinations — use Tabs/a horizontal menu.
sideNav.when1: The app has ≥5 destinations or needs a hierarchy
sideNav.when3: Narrow screens → collapse into an icon rail
sideNav.do1: Use sections to group related items, helping users scan quickly.
sideNav.do2: Place the user account at the bottom (avatar + name + email) — the app-shell standard.
sideNav.dont1: Placing the app title in the Side Nav when the Top Nav already carries the identity — duplicate branding.
sideNav.dont2: Using the Side Nav to filter content — use Tabs or a filter button for that.
sideNav.exEndD: Items with a badge, count and right-aligned trailing text. Click an item to change page; click the bell to see notifications.
sideNav.exNestedD: Items with sub-groups that expand/collapse on click; the group containing the selected item opens automatically. Click a sub-item to change page.
sideNav.exSwitchT: Side Nav — Switch account + user block
sideNav.exSwitchD: Top: an organization switcher (collapsed → just an icon, still opens a dropdown). Bottom: a user account block with a settings menu.
sideNav.exSearchD: Enable [searchable] → a search box at the top of the nav. Filters by label + related keywords, diacritics-insensitive. A matching parent shows all its sub-items; a matching child only opens its group.
sideNav.notifyLeave: Leave request — Trần Thu Hà awaiting approval
sideNav.title: Side Nav

topNav.desc: A product-level horizontal navigation bar at the top of the app: logo, primary items (≤5) and a search/actions area on the right.
topNav.ovNote: Logo + heading, navigation items, and account actions on the right (the “With logo” style).
topNav.purpose: Product-level horizontal navigation in the header — ≤5 destinations always visible, with search and actions.
topNav.behavior: Left: logo/brand. Center: items (which can be dropdowns/mega-menus). Right: a flexible area (search/buttons/avatar). The selected item is a pill.
topNav.avoid: Many destinations or a deep hierarchy — use Side Nav. Filtering content — use Tabs.
topNav.when1: The app has ≤5 primary destinations always visible
topNav.when2: The header needs search + account + a CTA
topNav.do1: Keep ≤5 items always visible; put secondary groups into a dropdown/mega-menu.
topNav.do2: Place search + account + CTA in the right area.
topNav.dont1: Cramming a hierarchical navigation tree into the top nav — use Side Nav.
topNav.exCenterD: Navigation items centered, logo on the left and actions on the right. Suits marketing/landing pages.
topNav.exEnterpriseD: Items with icon + label, plus a search box, a notification bell and a primary CTA button. A full admin-app header.
topNav.exMultiD: Several items open a dropdown on hover; moving between items opens/closes the menus automatically. A SaaS navigation style.
topNav.exHoverD: One item opens a menu on hover, listing products with an icon and a short description. Helps introduce them quickly.
topNav.exMegaD: A large, wide menu: a multi-column product grid plus a highlighted promo card. A marketing-page style.
topNav.promoDesc: An all-in-one HRM platform — 30-day free trial.

money.desc: A money input for HRM workflows: it inserts thousands separators automatically and attaches the currency unit.
money.purpose: Let users enter monetary amounts (salary, allowances, bonuses, expenses) in the correct, readable format.
money.behavior: As you type, it inserts thousands separators and shows the currency unit. It accepts digits only; on an invalid value, the border turns red.
money.avoid: Numbers that aren't money (quantities, age, leave days) — use a Number input.
money.when2: Declaring deductions and expenses in a form
money.when3: Any monetary field that needs thousands formatting
money.do1: Use it for every money field: salary, allowances, bonuses, deductions.
money.do2: Set the step to match real denominations — salary in thousands, allowances in hundreds of thousands.
money.do3: When the value is out of the allowed range, show a clear red state so the user can fix it.
money.dont1: Making users type the thousands separators themselves or type the word "dong".
money.exSalaryD: A base salary field in Vietnamese dong: type the number straight and the system adds thousands separators and the ₫ unit for readability.
money.exAllowD: An allowance field with a minimum and a step in hundreds of thousands — the arrows add/subtract by the exact denomination, avoiding a stray zero.
money.exStateD: Error, warning and success. Tell users what's wrong with the amount they entered — over the cap, needs review, or correct.
money.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for multi-row payroll sheets, medium for most forms, large for an approval page with one prominent amount.
money.title: Money

phone.desc: A phone number input for HRM workflows: it attaches a dial code, accepts digits only, and signals validity.
phone.purpose: Let users enter a contact phone number, with the country dial code already shown in front.
phone.behavior: The field always shows the dial code (default +84) in front. It accepts digits only — letters and stray characters are dropped as you type, up to 11 digits. Invalid turns the border red; valid turns it green.
phone.avoid: Any number that isn't a phone (tax code, account number) — use a regular input.
phone.when1: Phone number in an employee profile
phone.when3: A contact number for a relative/dependent
phone.do1: Use it for the phone field in employee profiles and emergency contacts.
phone.do2: Change the dial code to the right country when the employee is abroad (+84, +65, +81…).
phone.do3: Signal status clearly: red when the number is the wrong length, green when it's valid.
phone.dont1: Making users type the dial code into the number field — the dial code is already provided.
phone.dont2: Allowing letters or special characters in the phone number.
phone.exStaffD: A standard phone field with the Vietnam dial code (+84), accepting digits only. Use it for the contact field in an employee profile.
phone.exDialD: Change the dial code to the employee's country: Vietnam, Singapore, Japan. The dial code stays fixed at the front of the field.
phone.exStateD: Error when the number is the wrong length, warning when it needs review, and success when the number is correct. The colored border tells users at a glance whether the number is usable.
phone.exSizeD: Small, medium, large. Small for filters/dense tables, medium for most forms, large for a standout single-field page.
phone.title: Phone

loginPage.title: Login Page
loginPage.desc: A full-screen login template: VnResource green gradient background, login card on the right, testimonial on the left. Built from DS components + tokens.
loginPage.purpose: A standard app login screen: authenticate with email/password or SSO, with brand identity.
loginPage.behavior: Two areas: left = brand background (gradient + testimonial), right = login card (Google/Microsoft/LinkedIn SSO, email, password with show/hide, remember me, forgot password). Uses hrm-input, hrm-button, hrm-checkbox, hrm-divider.
loginPage.avoid: Cramming too many choices into one screen — keep login lean, move the rest to dedicated pages (Register, Forgot password).
loginPage.when1: Login screen of an internal application
loginPage.when3: A starting template for authentication pages
loginPage.do1: Use the correct brand color (logo) for the gradient and primary button.
loginPage.do2: Use original provider logos on SSO buttons so users recognize them instantly.
loginPage.dont1: Re-building your own input/button — use DS components to stay consistent with theme and error states.
loginPage.exFullD: Open in a new tab to see the true full-screen proportions. Route: /login (outside the styleguide shell).

listPage.title: Data Views
listPage.desc: Standard index screen: app shell + list panel + multiple data views (Table/Card/Board/Gantt) like ClickUp.
listPage.purpose: Give every list screen the same skeleton so teams build index pages fast and consistently.
listPage.when1: Screens showing a searchable, paginated table of records (employees, contracts, requests).
listPage.when2: Module index pages needing breadcrumb, title and a primary action in one place.
listPage.behavior: Composes breadcrumb, page header, toolbar, the projected grid and pagination with standard spacing. Columns, filters and buttons come from the caller via slots.
listPage.avoid: Detail or form screens, dashboards or wizard flows — this is for record lists only.
listPage.do1: Place it inside the app shell so the side nav stays shared, not duplicated.
listPage.do2: Set the grid to showPagination false and let the page's pagination drive paging.
listPage.dont1: Don't bake the side nav into the list page — the app shell already owns it.
listPage.exShellD: The complete list screen: side nav from the app shell plus the list-page section — the layout to reuse for every module index.
listPage.exMultiT: Data views — Table / Card / Board / Gantt
listPage.exMultiD: One dataset, many views like ClickUp. Switch via the tab bar; drag cards between Board columns.

quickFilter.title: Quick Filter
quickFilter.desc: Pill-style quick filter for toolbars — open a list, pick one or many, with a selection count.
quickFilter.purpose: Filter lists/tables right on the toolbar without opening the full filter panel. Compact pill, selection state visible in place.
quickFilter.when1: List-screen toolbars with 2–5 common criteria (department, status, language…)
quickFilter.when2: Short–medium option lists (≤ ~50 items), multi-tick or single pick
quickFilter.when3: You want active filters visible at a glance (brand border + count)
quickFilter.behavior: Click the pill to open a panel: search box (diacritics-insensitive) + Select all (multiple mode) + options. One selection shows its name; 2+ shows a bold "N units"; the pill border turns brand color. ✕ clears all. Single mode closes after picking.
quickFilter.avoid: Not for complex multi-field conditions (use the list-page Filter panel); not a replacement for Select inside data-entry forms.
quickFilter.do1: Set a meaningful unit ("2 languages", "3 departments") for fast reading
quickFilter.do2: Group 2–5 quick filters on one toolbar row; use single mode for mutually exclusive criteria (sort, status)
quickFilter.dont1: Don't stack >5 filter pills on one toolbar — switch to the full filter panel
quickFilter.dont2: Don't use multiple mode for criteria that only allow one value (sorting)
quickFilter.exMultiD: Tick many items — one selection shows its name, 2+ shows "N languages"; Select all shows a dash when partially selected.
quickFilter.exSingleD: Mutually exclusive criteria — closes after picking, the pill shows the current value.
quickFilter.exGroupD: Several quick filters side by side — one pill per criterion, independent state.

filterPanel.title: Filter Panel
filterPanel.desc: Builder-style advanced filter — each row: field · operator · value; add/remove conditions, commit with Apply (draft).
filterPanel.purpose: Gather several filter criteria in one vertical panel: collapsible groups, any DS control inside; apply once with the Apply button.
filterPanel.when1: List/report screens filtering by several fields at once (department + status + date range…)
filterPanel.when2: Avoid reloading data on every interaction — users finish editing, then Apply
filterPanel.when3: Complex criteria needing rich controls (range picker, slider, checkbox groups)
filterPanel.behavior: The button opens a panel: header (title + subtitle + ↺ Reset) · each row = field + operator + type-driven value control (text/select/multi-tags/date-range/segmented) · "+ Add condition" opens a searchable grouped field picker · footer Cancel / Reset / Apply. Draft: Apply commits into [(conditions)] and emits (apply); Cancel discards; Reset clears values keeping the panel open. The button badge counts applied conditions.
filterPanel.avoid: Not for 1–2 simple criteria (use Quick Filter, instant apply); never auto-commit the draft before Apply is pressed.
filterPanel.do1: Declare the fields config once — mark frequent fields visible, mandatory ones fixed
filterPanel.do2: Keep default operators per type unless business requires otherwise (pass operators)
filterPanel.dont1: Don't mix semantics: instant-apply controls inside a panel that has an Apply button
filterPanel.dont2: Don't make too many fields visible by default — 4–6, the rest live in the picker
filterPanel.demoNote: Edit conditions then press Apply — applied conditions
filterPanel.exToolbarD: Quick Filters (instant) for common criteria + Filter Panel (draft) for the advanced part — AlignUI's Horizontal Filter pattern.
filterPanel.demoSub: Filter employees by the criteria you choose
